tools.name: check
tools.description:
check(subject="acme-agent", rule="at least 90% of at least 50 settled jobs") → signed ALLOW or REFUSE. Try check(subject="try-me") first.
Call before you pay, hire, or allocate to any agent, service or company. Returns one signed verdict (mizan.verdict/1): decision ALLOW or REFUSE first, then the gr

tools.name: require
tools.description:
require(words="at least 90% of at least 50 settled jobs") → the exact rule, its read-back and hash; then check(subject, rule=<the rule>).
Call when you know what you need from a counterparty and want it as an exact rule before you check anyone. Write the bar in plain words (words=...) or as structur

tools.name: prove
tools.description:
prove(claim_type="model_eval", ...) or prove(positions=[...], dataset="btc_4h") → your record, counted; previews are free and private.
Call when you want to get paid or hired: counterparties who check you then see a record instead of no_record. Prove the claim, never the method: your model, code and

tools.name: more
tools.description:
more("verify") · more("standard") · more("log") · more("problems") → every other tool by job, callable here by name.
Call when check, require, prove and claim_identity are not the job: verify a credential someone shows you, the published standard and its gates, the public log and receipts, linking y

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: check · Private data: check, prove, more · Public sink: check.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: check · Private data: check, prove, more · Public sink: check

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
